subject: arts-and-music
unit_title: Advanced Studio Technique and Materials
title: Launch and diagnostic: sustained technique development
standards: Michigan Arts Education Standards: Visual Arts — Creating
essential_question: How far can a material be pushed before technique becomes the idea?
learning_objectives: Surface what is already known about sustained technique development without penalty and establish the unit question.
Communicate understanding of sustained technique development using subject-appropriate evidence or representation.
Check, revise, or improve the work on sustained technique development against the stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task on sustained technique development.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name a next step.
materials: sketchbook and course notebook or digital equivalent
unit-appropriate safe studio materials and tools
original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved reference works only

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a brief, accessible prompt on sustained technique development. Ask the learner to notice, predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.

Observe closely, demonstrate the technique, let the learner work from direct observation or a developed idea, then revise from one specific criteria-based piece of feedback. Keep the work centred on sustained technique development, name the success criteria, and model how to check the result.
Work through supported examples of sustained technique development, fading prompts as the learner takes over. After each move ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that?”

Learner records current thinking about sustained technique development — a prediction, a sketch, a first attempt, or a set of questions — before any instruction. Nothing here is scored for correctness.
Name one thing you already understand about sustained technique development and one thing you want resolved by the end of the unit.

student_activity: Learner records current thinking about sustained technique development — a prediction, a sketch, a first attempt, or a set of questions — before any instruction. Nothing here is scored for correctness.
formative_check: Name one thing you already understand about sustained technique development and one thing you want resolved by the end of the unit.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for sustained technique development, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to sustained technique development works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of sustained technique development, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: requests the answer to graded work
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking sustained technique development mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use sketch or rehearsal record, created or performed work, artist statement, critique response, revision log, and portfolio reflection; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply sustained technique development under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting sustained technique development.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

study_integration.artifact_persistence: Persist a safe reference and metadata only: artifact type, learner-supplied title, family-chosen storage location, completion state, rubric evidence, and revision count. Do not store raw learner artifacts, media, recordings, or full project files in the study record unless host storage explicitly supports it.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one thing worth looking at more slowly, and record it in the sketchbook. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or private disclosure is required.

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a brief, accessible prompt on presentation and feedback cycle. Ask the learner to notice, predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.

Learner works two further supported examples of presentation and feedback cycle under a changed constraint, with prompts faded on the second.

formative_check: State how the changed constraint altered your approach to presentation and feedback cycle.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for presentation and feedback cycle, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.

Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.

learning_objectives: Demonstrate current mastery across portfolio, artist statement, and critical review, showing process or evidence for each response.
Communicate understanding of portfolio, artist statement, and critical review using subject-appropriate evidence or representation.
Check, revise, or improve the work on portfolio, artist statement, and critical review against the stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task on portfolio, artist statement, and critical review.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name a next step.
materials: portfolio folder, box, or digital equivalent
documentation setup — artwork only, no person in frame
rights and permissions log; artist statement drafts

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a brief, accessible prompt on portfolio, artist statement, and critical review. Ask the learner to notice, predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.

Curate rather than accumulate: select against explicit criteria, sequence for coherence, document accurately, and write about the work in plain language. Keep the work centred on portfolio, artist statement, and critical review, name the success criteria, and model how to check the result.
Work through supported examples of portfolio, artist statement, and critical review, fading prompts as the learner takes over. After each move ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that?”
Learner completes the unit assessment covering portfolio, artist statement, and critical review, working independently and showing process or evidence for each response.
Identify the item you are least confident about and say what would resolve it.

student_activity: Learner completes the unit assessment covering portfolio, artist statement, and critical review, working independently and showing process or evidence for each response.
formative_check: Identify the item you are least confident about and say what would resolve it.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for portfolio, artist statement, and critical review, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to portfolio, artist statement, and critical review works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of portfolio, artist statement, and critical review, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: requests the answer to graded work
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking portfolio, artist statement, and critical review mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use sketch or rehearsal record, created or performed work, artist statement, critique response, revision log, and portfolio reflection; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply portfolio, artist statement, and critical review under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting portfolio, artist statement, and critical review.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

study_integration.artifact_persistence: Persist a safe reference and metadata only: artifact type, learner-supplied title, family-chosen storage location, completion state, rubric evidence, and revision count. Do not store raw learner artifacts, media, recordings, or full project files in the study record unless host storage explicitly supports it.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to choose one piece of your own work and say in one sentence why it belongs. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or private disclosure is required.
